title.narrative: Urban Programme: New Media and Youth Engagement

description.narrative:
The Urban Programme aims to improve housing and basic services for families living in the shanty towns and tenements of São Paulo, through advocacy, campaigning and grassroots capacity building with a particular focus on women and young people.
Young people have traditionally been “early adopters” of technology. CAFOD has been conversing with the UP coordinators over the past two years about how best to take advantage of these trends. In squatter communities, people are very present on Orkut – the largest social network in Brazil, and spontaneously share videos and experiences in their lives as squatters. Social media is a way of linking beneficiaries and implementers, and creating an organic sense of accountability between our partners and those they work with and serve. During visits in the first two years of the programme, there was recognition by all in the UP of the need to change their approach to and develop more innovative ways of engaging young people in the UP and in the fight for social inclusion. We feel that the use of new media could be a cost effective way to engage young people and will have more impact by reaching a larger audience.
Objectives: 1. Empowered youth in the Programme see themselves as the drivers of change and source of renewal for the housing movement – concerns and issues of youth beneficiaries are expressed so that the UP can be more accountable to them 2. Increased profile of the Programme and the issues it addresses in relation to the major media and the middle class, enabling the Programme to achieve greater policy influence 3. The benefits of better communication and sharing of experience between UP partners – facilitated by horizontal linking of partner representatives and their activists using social media 4. Integration and improvement of online presence of the Urban Programme and its various partners and beneficiaries.
